headline: 115 days stranded: 17 Bangladeshi sailors return home from Hormuz
summary: The crew members were stuck in the Strait of Hormuz for nearly four months before finally reuniting with their families in Bangladesh.
details: Seventeen Bangladeshi sailors have finally returned home after being stranded in the Strait of Hormuz for 115 days.
The sailors had been stuck in the region for nearly four months, facing uncertainty and isolation from their families.
Upon their arrival at the airport, they were greeted by their loved ones and officials, marking the end of a long period of distress.
The return of the crew members follows diplomatic efforts to secure their release and repatriation to Bangladesh.
caption:
Stranded for 115 days in the Strait of Hormuz, 17 Bangladeshi sailors have finally returned home.

Seventeen Bangladeshi sailors have finally returned home after being stranded in the Strait of Hormuz for 115 days.

The sailors had been stuck in the region for nearly four months, facing uncertainty and isolation from their families.

Upon their arrival at the airport, they were greeted by their loved ones and officials, marking the end of a long period of distress.

The return of the crew members follows diplomatic efforts to secure their release and repatriation to Bangladesh.

#Bangladesh #Hormuz #Sailors #Repatriation #WorldNews

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune

headline: JU suspends 8 students over ragging allegations
summary: Jagannath University takes strict action against students accused of ragging, emphasizing a zero-tolerance policy toward harassment.
details: Jagannath University (JU) has suspended eight students following allegations of ragging. The university administration has taken this step to ensure a safe environment for newcomers.
The suspensions come after reports of harassment and intimidation of junior students by their seniors.
The university has reiterated its commitment to a zero-tolerance policy regarding ragging, stating that such behavior is strictly prohibited on campus.
The administration is conducting a further investigation into the incidents to determine if more students are involved or if further disciplinary action is required.
caption:
8 students suspended at Jagannath University. Ragging allegations spark immediate action.

Jagannath University (JU) has suspended eight students following allegations of ragging. The university administration has taken this step to ensure a safe environment for newcomers.

The suspensions come after reports of harassment and intimidation of junior students by their seniors.

The university has reiterated its commitment to a zero-tolerance policy regarding ragging, stating that such behavior is strictly prohibited on campus.

The administration is conducting a further investigation into the incidents to determine if more students are involved or if further disciplinary action is required.

Source: Dhaka Tribune
